# Focused strace with -e trace Filters

## Thesis

**`strace`** is only useful when the noise is gone. `-e trace=` (and friends) cut the stream to the syscalls you care about — file opens, network, signals — so a short reproduction stays readable.

## Mental model

```text
  strace -e trace=openat,close       # only those syscalls
  strace -e trace=%file              # class: file ops
  strace -e trace=%network           # class: socket ops
  strace -f                          # follow children
  strace -o out.txt                  # don't mix with program stdout
```

Classes (`%file`, `%network`, `%process`, `%signal`, …) are listed in `man strace`.

## Worked example

`strace` is **not installed** on this writing box (policy: no package installs). The patterns below are from the strace man page and everyday ops practice; run them on a lab host that has `strace`.

```bash
# What files does `ls /tmp` touch?
strace -e trace=openat,close -o /tmp/ls.strace ls /tmp >/dev/null
head /tmp/ls.strace

# Network-only view of a curl
strace -f -e trace=%network -o /tmp/curl.strace curl -s -o /dev/null https://example.com

# Failed opens only (path bugs)
strace -e trace=openat -e fault=openat:error=ENOENT:when=1  # advanced; see man
strace -e trace=openat -Y true  # decode paths; version-dependent
```

Typical `openat` lines look like:

```text
openat(AT_FDCWD, "/etc/ld.so.cache", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) = 3
openat(AT_FDCWD, "/tmp", O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK|O_CLOEXEC|O_DIRECTORY) = 3
```

## Trap

**`strace -f` on a production service under load.** Every syscall traps into the tracer; latency explodes. Prefer a short reproduction, `perf`, or eBPF for live systems. Also: tracing secrets-handling processes can spill passwords into the log — redirect to a protected file.

## Boring rule

Start with `-e trace=` for one class or a short syscall list, always `-o` a file, add `-f` only when children matter, and stop as soon as you have the failing path or errno.

## Try this

1. Compare `-e trace=%file` vs listing `openat,stat,statx` explicitly.
2. Use `-e write=all -e read=all` carefully to dump buffer contents for a small repro only.
3. When `strace` is unavailable, read `/proc/<pid>/fd` and `/proc/<pid>/stack` as a lighter first pass.
